CAPACITOR IDENTIFICATION
OBJECTIVES
w Identify ceramic, film, mica, and electrolytic capacitors.
w Read the capacitance and voltage values......................
EQUIPMENT REQUIRED
Nida Experiment Card PC130 - 11
The physical appearance of capacitors vary.
INTRODUCTIONM
The most common capacitors are identified by the type of dielectric used.
Almost all capacitors have their capacitance values and voltage ratings printed on the body. Electrolytic Ceramic Film Mica 470
In rare cases, a color code is used to identify the capacitance value and voltage rating.
Capacitor color codes are not as standard as those used for resistors. Refer to a capacitor reference book to determine value and voltage rating for color coded capacitors.
Let's begin the lesson on CAPACITOR IDENTIFICATION........................
LESSON MENU
The PC130-11 has six capacitors labeled C1 through C6 and are identified as either electrolytic, ceramic, film, or mica.
EXPERIMENT
There are two electrolytic capacitors, C1 and C2.
The small capacitor labeled C3 is a ceramic capacitor.
There are also two film capacitors, C4 and C5.
The last capacitor, C6, is a mica capacitor.
Look at the capacitor C5. This film capacitor uses a dielectric material similar to wax paper.
Manufacturers use different ways to indicate the value of capacitors.

Let's look at the capacitor on the left. Its value is .33 microfarads. Film capacitors normally have values in the microfarad range, so we can assume that the value is in microfarads unless indicated otherwise....
The capacitor on the right uses a three digit code to identify its value. This code expresses the capacitor's value in picofarads.
The first two digits are the significant digits and the third is the multiplier.
To find the capacitor's value, multiply the significant digits and the multiplier. 10000 Multiplier x 33 Significant Digits
Capacitors also have tolerance ratings. The ratings can be printed on the capacitor or a code is used.
When the tolerance is not printed on the capacitor, manufacturers will use codes. A k is used to indicate a

The DC voltage rating can be identified by a V. Sometimes a manufacturer's code is used.
Manufacturers use different codes for the same voltage ratings. It may be necessary to reference the manufacturer's specifications in order to identify the code.
Capacitor C3 is called a "ceramic" capacitor because the dielectric used is ceramic.
Common values for ceramic capacitors range from picofarads to around 0.5MF (microfarads).

The value is printed on the capacitor and followed by a unit such as M (microfarad). The M indicates the unit m (microfarad). This should not be confused with Mega since the value of ceramic capacitors does not exceed 1 farad...
Some ceramic capacitors use a three digit code to indicate their value.
The first two digits are the significant digits and the third is the multiplier. This capacitor has a value of .01mF. 1000 Multiplier x 10 Significant Digits
The voltage rating is printed on ceramic capacitors in the same manner as the Mica capacitor.
It is not unusual for a voltage rating not to be printed on a ceramic cap. If this is the case, you will have to reference schematics or a parts manual to determine the voltage rating.

Additionally, the arrow with the "-" symbol indicates the negative end.
All electrolytic capacitors have one or more indicators for the positive and negative ends.
